c.tagline: Shikoku's gateway city — sanuki udon, a strolling garden, and ferries to the art islands.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and plentiful; ride-hailing (GO, DiDi) only dispatches licensed metered taxis rather than private cars, and street and rank taxis are easy to find.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance; English support is limited, so the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) offers 24/7 multilingual help.

hood_desc: The waterfront hub around JR Takamatsu Station and Sunport, with the ferry terminal for the art islands, symbol tower, and Tamamo Park next door; best for first-timers who want transport and ferries on the doorstep.

Downtown Takamatsu's shopping and nightlife core, threaded by the long covered Marugamemachi and Hyogomachi arcades and centered on Kawaramachi station; suits travelers who want restaurants, bars, and shopping at hand.
A calmer district around the celebrated Ritsurin Garden, one of Japan's finest strolling gardens, with quiet residential streets and teahouses; good for a slower, greener stay.
The historic core beside Takamatsu Castle (Tamamo Park), a rare seawater-moated castle by the port; a compact, sightseeing-focused pocket steps from the station.
A residential area on the city's eastern edge below the flat-topped Yashima plateau, site of a famous 12th-century battle, temples, and sweeping Inland Sea views; quiet and local.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Japan.

transit.hours: Kotoden trains and city buses run from roughly 5:30 AM to 11:00 PM; there is no night service, so late trips rely on taxis.
transit.note: Takamatsu's local rail is the Kotoden (Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad), whose three lines — Kotohira, Nagao, and Shido — fan out from the central Kawaramachi and Takamatsu-Chikko hubs, backed by Kotoden city buses, JR Shikoku trains, and Seto Inland Sea ferries from Takamatsu Port to the art islands.
transit.pay: Tap a nationwide IC card or Kotoden's own IruCa card on trains and buses (a city ride is around ¥200, ~US$1.40); cash is also accepted onboard.

bus: Highway buses to Okayama, Kobe, Osaka & Tokyo
ferry: Takamatsu Port (ferries to Naoshima, Teshima, Shodoshima, Megijima, Ogijima & Uno/Okayama)

transit.m: Airport Limousine Bus to JR Takamatsu Station (~40 min, ¥1000)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is standard and already included.
